solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dying tissue effectively consumes radius

indicators.note: what consumes something takes it inside itself, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: 'in fact' means effectively, in reality
R is the standard abbreviation for radius

explanation.surface: A medical note: dying tissue is in effect eating into a bone of the forearm.
explanation.walkthrough: The radius is a forearm bone, which keeps the medical surface going, but here it is only the abbreviation R, set inside IN FACT to make INFARCT.
explanation.definitionFit: An infarct is a localised area of dead tissue caused by a blocked blood supply.

clue.text: Dutch river needing not so much sail trimmed, hoisted?

indicators.note: in a down clue, hoisting lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
trimmed means cut at the edge, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: less means not so much
a jib is a triangular sail at the front of a boat

explanation.surface: A barge on a Dutch river needs less sail, so the canvas is trimmed and raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoisting in a down clue sends the letters upward. The IJ at the start counts as a single letter in Dutch, which is why the name looks so strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The IJssel is a branch of the Rhine flowing north through the Netherlands into the IJsselmeer.

clue.text: Female name overlooked in conservative shock of shocks?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: something overlooked in a word is left out of it, so that letter is missed

parts.note: right-wing means politically conservative
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman is passed over by a conservative party, which comes as the greatest shock of all.
explanation.walkthrough: N comes out of RIGHT WING. In the definition a 'shock' of hair stands up as if shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright wig is a wig with hair standing on end, as worn by clowns, so it is a shock of hair styled like a fright.

clue.text: Head of Rolling Stone welcoming a funny staff writer

indicators.note: the outer letters welcome the next piece in, taking it inside them
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Rolling
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds
rum means odd, funny-peculiar
taken as written

explanation.surface: The editor of Rolling Stone magazine takes on a humorous member of the writing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff writer' sounds like a journalist on Rolling Stone, but the staff is the five-line musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: A rastrum is a five-pointed pen used to rule the lines of a musical stave in one stroke.

clue.text: Slips with religious texts mostly working round NT book

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: tilling means working the soil
Eph is the abbreviation for Ephesians, a New Testament book

explanation.surface: Someone makes errors while busy with scripture, mostly in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' looks like a verb about mistakes, but it is the definition, slips of parchment carrying scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tephillin are the small leather boxes containing parchment slips of Torah verses, worn by observant Jewish men at prayer.

clue.text: Critically alter modern concert repertoire, consistently cutting finishing time

indicators.note: the closing letter standing for time is removed, and 'consistently' says this happens to both words alike

parts.note: modern means recent
a band's set is the list of numbers it plays at a concert

explanation.surface: A conductor is told to overhaul a modern concert programme, always trimming the end so the evening runs shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: T is time, and both RECENT and SET end in it, so each loses its final T to give RECEN + SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recense is to revise a text critically, producing a new recension of it.

clue.text: Splendid non-professional people without commission turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lay people are non-professionals, outside a profession
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who hold no officer's commission

explanation.surface: Amateurs who were not paid any fee have arrived, and it is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without commission' sounds like no sales fee, but it means not commissioned as officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal can mean magnificent or fit for a king, as in a royal welcome.

clue.text: Fantastic cosplay as character from Odyssey

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and wildly made-up, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan dresses up superbly as a figure from Homer's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: Cosplay is dressing as a fictional character, which fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is the nymph in Homer's Odyssey who keeps Odysseus on her island for seven years.

clue.text: Nickel-plated iron supplying people of southern Africa

indicators.note: a plating is a coat over the outside, so the first piece covers the second all round

parts.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
iron is slang for a handgun

explanation.surface: Nickel-coated iron is what is being sold to the people of southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' is the metal in the surface but slang for a gun in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nguni are a group of Bantu-speaking peoples of southern Africa including the Zulu, Xhosa and Swazi.

clue.text: Radical redesign for cell units

indicators.note: a radical change is a thorough overhaul, so the letters are rearranged completely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect proposes a sweeping redesign of the cells in a prison block.
explanation.definitionFit: An energid is a nucleus with the cytoplasm it governs, regarded as a functional unit within a cell.

clue.text: Nothing in old physics represented astrology etc

indicators.note: something represented is presented again in a new form, so the letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
O is the dictionary abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist sneers that astrology and its kind are nothing but old physics dressed up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing in old physics' reads like a dismissive verdict, but it supplies two Os to add to the seven letters of PHYSICS before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciosophy is a supposed system of knowledge with no scientific basis, such as astrology or other occult lore.

clue.text: Bound to receive superior instrument in view of fine work

definitions.text: instrument in view of fine work

indicators.note: one word receives another, taking it in among its own letters

parts.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides
U means upper-class, superior in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone seems certain to be given a top-class tool for intricate work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to', but Bound is a leap, LOPE, which receives U for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A loupe is a small magnifying glass held to the eye by jewellers and watchmakers doing delicate work.

clue.text: Maybe Guy's Hospital in backing for Greek legal administrator

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the assembled letters are read from the end
with the possessive read as 'has', the first word has the next one in it, inside its letters

parts.note: a guy is a rope steadying a tent or mast, so 'maybe' marks it as one example of a rope
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

explanation.surface: Guy's is a London teaching hospital, here apparently sponsoring a Greek legal official.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a famous London hospital, but the words split: a guy is a rope, the 's is 'has', and ROPE has H inside it before the whole reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephors were the five magistrates elected each year in ancient Sparta to oversee the kings and the law.

clue.text: Sovereign is pallidly, somewhat contrarily, gliding in

indicators.note: acting contrarily means going the opposite way, so the run of letters is read backwards
somewhat means to some degree, so only part of the run of words is taken

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A monarch is described as pale and rather stubborn, an odd portrait of a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards inside 'sovereiGN IS PALLIdly'; read them from the end to get ILLAPSING.
explanation.definitionFit: To illapse is a rare verb meaning to slip or glide gently into something, so illapsing is gliding in.

clue.text: Women's walk cut short for some suffering indigestion?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on lavatory doors
an amble is a leisurely walk
hair or grass cut short is cropped

explanation.surface: A women's walking event is curtailed because some of the walkers have upset stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' looks like an instruction to delete letters, but it is the plain word CROPPED, the last third of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wamble-cropped is an old dialect adjective for someone queasy and sick in the stomach, wamble being a rumbling of the gut.

clue.text: University's river and the one it joins, not SE London's old one, short of English mine

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge

indicators.note: not here means without, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: the Cam is a tributary of the Great Ouse
taken as written

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the word goes without the named letter

parts.note: the Fleet is a London river long since buried underground
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tour of rivers: Cambridge's, the one it flows into, and London's lost one, ending at an English mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The SE printed in the clue is what the Ouse loses. The Fleet is a London river now buried and running in sewers.
explanation.definitionFit: A camouflet is an underground mine or explosion that does not break the surface, used to collapse enemy tunnels.

clue.text: Ruffling waspy Josh, a matchmaker's occupational hazard?

indicators.note: ruffling disorders something, as wind does hair, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Annoying a prickly man called Josh is the risk a romantic go-between runs.
explanation.walkthrough: A matchmaker here is not a romantic go-between but a worker making matches in a match factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Phossy jaw was bone decay of the jaw caused by white phosphorus, an industrial disease of Victorian match-factory workers.

clue.text: Illegitimate Jews married in confusion, on edge

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, set among its letters

parts.note: a maze is a state of bewilderment
M is the abbreviation for married
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Jewish children born out of wedlock are wed in a muddle, everyone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but in a down clue 'on' just places the edge after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish law a mamzer is a child of a forbidden union such as adultery; mamzerim is the Hebrew plural.

clue.text: Updating past to include private embellishment

indicators.note: the first word is made to include the rest, wrapping around them

parts.note: ago means in the past
a GI is an American private soldier
an ornament is an embellishment

explanation.surface: A homeowner modernises an old house by adding a personal decorative touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The past word opens after its first letter to take in the rest. 'Private' is the soldier, not secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggiornamento is the Italian word for bringing up to date, used especially of the reforms of the Second Vatican Council.

clue.text: Party animal also known as the wrong Pole aboard Jumbo?

indicators.note: having the wrong one means the correct letter is swapped out for its opposite

parts.note: or introduces an alternative name, as in 'Mumbai, or Bombay'
jumbo means giant-sized
S, south, is the other pole from the N that Jumbo's letters hold

explanation.surface: An elephant at a party is said to have the wrong Polish person on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: The north pole N in GIANT is replaced by the opposite pole S.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgiast is someone who takes part in orgies, a wild reveller.

clue.text: Gluten-free powder in fruitcake, a serving of food

parts.note: a fruitcake and a nut are both slang for an eccentric person
a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: A recipe uses a wheat-free flour in fruitcake, which makes a portion of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' is the cake in the surface but slang for a crazy person in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeal is finely ground nuts, used in baking as a flour without wheat.

clue.text: Reveal antique lacework after lifting beam

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read upward

parts.note: a web is a fine lacy network
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A dealer uncovers old lace after hoisting a ceiling timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antique' looks like it describes the lacework, but it belongs to the definition, marking the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewray is an obsolete verb meaning to divulge or betray a secret, so it is an old word for reveal.

clue.text: Variable height on both sides of English, French or Chinese city

indicators.note: a piece placed on both sides of another appears once before it and once after it, surrounding it

parts.note: the same pair again, for the far side
ou is the French word for or
Eng is the abbreviation for English
Z is a standard symbol for a variable and H the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A list of cities with the height above sea level and names given in English, French or Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: ZH is written twice, once on each side of ENG, and the French word for 'or' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zhengzhou is the capital of Henan province in central China.

clue.text: Raised floor decoration that needs a special viewer

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that needs one

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters go upward, read from the bottom

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, a KO
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An elevated floor with ornamentation that can only be appreciated with a special viewing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor decoration' suggests a mosaic, but floor is the boxing KO and decoration the OBE medal, read upward together.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is a book in digital form, read on a dedicated reader device or app.

clue.text: Who's struck roadside, shifting feet?

indicators.note: the feet of words in a down clue are their last letters, and shifting them means moving them away

parts.note: struck means hit
the kerb is the British spelling of curb, the edge of the pavement

explanation.surface: Someone at the side of the road, shuffling their sore feet, wonders who has been hit.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT and KERB each lose their last letter. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a walker on the roadside moving on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is a walker covering distance on foot, often along roads and verges.

clue.text: On the evidence of affluent travellers, judge struck back

indicators.note: going back means reading the remaining letters from the end
struck off means removed, as a name is struck from a list

parts.note: the jet set are wealthy people who fly about the world
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge, having heard evidence from wealthy globetrotters, is attacked in return.
explanation.walkthrough: JET SET loses its J and the rest reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Teste is Latin used in English for citing a witness, meaning on the testimony of the person named.

clue.text: Australian native returning in the role of oil producer

parts.note: roo is Australian slang for a kangaroo

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the following short word is read from its end

parts.note: 'as' means in the role of, as in 'acting as host'

explanation.surface: An Aboriginal Australian comes home to work in the oil industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests a person, but it is the kangaroo. Only AS is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosa is an Indian grass whose leaves are distilled to yield an aromatic oil, so the plant is a producer of oil.

clue.text: Firing chamber shortened before clash, which is useful for preservation

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing that is useful

indicators.note: something shortened loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a kiln is an oven for firing pottery
ere is an old word for before
to jar is to clash, as colours or sounds do

explanation.surface: A potter's kiln is cut down in size before a row breaks out, though it still has its uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' sits after 'Firing chamber' but trims the word after it, ERE. A Kilner jar is a British brand of glass jar with a sealed lid, used for preserving fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilner jars are airtight glass containers made for bottling and pickling, so their purpose is preserving food.

clue.text: Turkish chief about to yield to king in a lot of paying stuff?

indicators.note: a letter that yields to another gives up its place, which the other then takes

parts.note: much means a lot of
c is short for circa, about
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to pay a ship's seams is to coat them with tar or pitch

explanation.surface: A Turkish leader is about to give way to a king over a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paying stuff' suggests cash, but to pay in nautical terms is to seal with tar. In MUCH, the C gives way to K.
explanation.definitionFit: A mukhtar is the elected headman of a village or neighbourhood in Turkey and the Arab world.

clue.text: Sailing vessel with fortune reversed where one pays for US passage

definitions.text: where one pays for US passage

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the joined pieces are read from the end

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A sailor whose luck has turned must pay their fare to cross to America.
explanation.walkthrough: YAWL + LOT is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollway is the American name for a highway on which drivers must pay a fee to travel.
